主要内容: PolarityTE, a biotech company based in Salt Lake City, disclosed on Monday that it is under investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for possible violations of securities laws, including anti-price manipulation provisions of the Exchange Act. The SEC issued a subpoena earlier this month, requesting additional documents related to its lead product, SkinTE, and communications with former executives and investors. The company's shares fell over 15% following the disclosure. The SEC declined to comment, and PolarityTE stated it intends to fully cooperate with the investigation. The subpoena also included requests for communications and agreements between the company and its former CFO, John Stetson, former CEO and current investor Barry Honig, and investor Michael Brauser. The company previously made video games before changing its name and business plan in January 2017. The SEC previously charged Honig, Brauser, and Stetson in connection with a $27 million market manipulation case, which was unrelated to PolarityTE. Biotech shares experienced a significant decline following reports that the SEC is investigating potential manipulation. Polarity, a biotech company, stated that its securities have been targeted by "short and distort" trader attacks, including the dissemination of false information on internet platforms. The company terminated its relationship with Stetson in response to these allegations. Honig and Brauser, who own nearly 7% of Polarity shares, are also linked to the case. Additionally, Riot Blockchain, a cryptocurrency company, has faced an ongoing SEC subpoena since last year, with its former CEO, John O'Rourke, charged alongside Honig in a microcap securities case. A CNBC investigation highlighted several red flags at Riot Blockchain, including delayed annual meetings, insider stock sales, and suspicious SEC filings.
